The proposed profile has close prior art: a 2022 content-recommendation study explicitly averages TF-IDF scores for terms appearing in at least two history documents, closely matching recurrence across distinct items ([paper](https://www.sciencedirect.com/org/science/article/pii/S2334454722000235)). Temporal user profiles and decay weighting also have established precedents ([temporal-profile study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11257-022-09354-7)). Corpus-level rare-term filtering is standard `min_df` preprocessing; it differs from requiring recurrence within one user’s history ([documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)). These findings suggest limited novelty in the ingredients; any contribution would need evidence for their particular combination or integration with sequential recommendation.

Useful low-cost comparators: normalized TF-IDF history centroid; exponential-recency centroid; last-item similarity; recurrence-filtered centroid; and SASRec blended with each content score. Ablate corpus frequency thresholds separately from user-history recurrence, and compare title-only versus title-plus-description. A learned global term-weighting comparator has direct precedent in [Content-Based Top-N Recommendation using Heterogeneous Relations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08104). These are proposed comparisons, without evidence yet that they improve this Amazon benchmark.

For learned text encoders, compare randomly initialized mean-pooled word embeddings plus a projection against a small CNN/GRU, keeping the interaction backbone and training objective fixed. [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.02116) compares averaging and recurrent encoders, but its reported experiments pretrained word embeddings on 440,756 ACM abstracts and optionally used tag supervision. Its gains therefore do not establish superiority under this task’s no-pretrained-weights and restricted-metadata conditions. Word order inside descriptions and chronological order of interacted items should be evaluated separately.
